title: Superlinear Wire Lower Bounds for Gates of Fan-In N^(1-delta)
description: For every delta > 0, a language in E^NP needs more than c(delta) N sqrt(log N) wires in circuits of any depth on N inputs whose gates are arbitrary Boolean functions of at most N^(1-delta) inputs, or threshold, exact, modular or symmetric gates of any fan-in with weights of at most N^(1-delta) bits. The proof extends the tensor-network contraction theorem of OpenAI from degree s^(9/10) to degree s^(1-delta) and counts the satisfying inputs of such circuits in time 2^(O(s/sqrt(log s))). An unconditional theorem shows that tree encodings of weighted gates need degree close to the weight length. The archive contains the paper, a Lean 4 project (46 theorems, standard axioms only) and Julia programs (44 checks). The P versus NP problem remains open.
